title: APPL_COLS referenced but never defined — ReferenceError on every openLocation()
detail: Line 473 builds the appliances $select clause via template literal `?$select=${APPL_COLS}&$expand=...`, but APPL_COLS is never defined or imported anywhere in the file. The first time a user taps a location in the field-ops view, openLocation() runs Promise.allSettled with this URL and the apiGet call will throw `ReferenceError: APPL_COLS is not defined` at the URL-build step (before the network call even fires). Promise.allSettled swallows it as a rejected entry, so the appliances state silently stays empty and no toast surfaces — the appliance grid will appear blank and the user has no idea why. Hard breakage of the entire field-ops appliance flow.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:473 — `apiGet(`/${EntitySets.appliances}?$select=${APPL_COLS}&$expand=dcfg_appliance_type_id($select=dcfg_name,dcfg_icon,dcfg_expected_lifespan_years)&$filter=_dcfg_property_id_value eq ${propertyId} and dcfg_is_active eq true&$orderby=dcfg_location_in_property asc`)`. Grep across LocationManager.jsx finds APPL_COLS only on this single line; no const/let/var/import declares it.
recommendedFix: Define an APPL_COLS constant near the DETAIL_COLS block (lines 53-64) listing every appliance column read by normaliseAppl() at line 146-162: `const APPL_COLS = 'dcfg_applianceid,dcfg_custom_label,dcfg_brand,dcfg_location_in_property,dcfg_install_date,dcfg_serial_number,dcfg_primary_photo_url,dcfg_serial_photo_url,dcfg_replace_by_status,dcfg_estimated_replace_by';` Verify by tapping any property in the field-ops view (`/#/field`) on Test and confirming the appliance list loads without console errors. Cross-check the column list against the 4 explicit-list table rule — dcfg_appliances is NOT in the 4 explicit-list tables on Prod, so wildcard would also work, but explicit $select is still preferred per pick-lane discipline.

title: apiPost called with 3rd arg + treated as if it returns the created record
detail: Line 555: `const created = await apiPost(`/${EntitySets.appliances}`, body, true);` — the third argument `true` is silently ignored because apiPost in portalApi.js (line 159) only accepts (path, body) and returns nothing (it does `if (!resp.ok) throw …` then falls off the bottom with no return statement). The very next line tries to read `created?.dcfg_applianceid`, which is always undefined, so the new appliance card created in setAppliances at line 563 always has id/guid = undefined. Subsequent debounced PATCH attempts keyed off that undefined GUID will fail or no-op. Photo upload at line 559 also passes undefined as the appliance_id. The author clearly intended apiPostReturn (which returns the created record).
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:555-556: `const created = await apiPost(`/${EntitySets.appliances}`, body, true); const newGuid = created?.dcfg_applianceid;` portalApi.js:159 `export async function apiPost(path, body) { ... }` (no return statement, no third param).
recommendedFix: Replace `apiPost` with `apiPostReturn` (already imported pattern in portalApi.js for tables that need the created record back) and drop the spurious `true` arg: `const created = await apiPostReturn(`/${EntitySets.appliances}`, body); const newGuid = created?.dcfg_applianceid;` Then verify by adding an appliance via the field-ops view and confirming the new card has a real GUID (visible in subsequent PATCH calls in network tab).

title: userName destructured from usePortalUser() but no such property exists
detail: Line 354: `const { userEmail, userName } = usePortalUser();`. usePortalUser returns the context shape from PortalUserContext, which exposes `user`, `loading`, `hasRole`, `isAdmin`, `isManager`, `isViewer`, `userEmail` — but NOT `userName`. (The user's display name lives at `user.name`.) As a result, every reference to `userName` in this file resolves to undefined: line 1099 `userName?.split(' ').map(...)` always falls back to 'FT' avatar initials and the avatar is always wrong for the field-ops user.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:354 destructures userName from usePortalUser; usePortalUser.jsx:67-71 returns `{ user, loading, ...makeRoleHelpers(user) }` where makeRoleHelpers exposes hasRole/isAdmin/isManager/isViewer/userEmail (line 110-116). LocationManager.jsx:1099 `userName?.split(' ').map(w => w[0]).join('').slice(0, 2) || 'FT'`
recommendedFix: Change destructure to pull the user object and read `user?.name`: `const { user, userEmail } = usePortalUser(); const userName = user?.name;` (and update line 1099 reference to use that local). Alternatively, expose `userName` from usePortalUser directly to mirror userEmail — but that requires a small portalUser change and is the broader fix; LocationManager-only fix is the safer Phase 5 option.

title: Hardcoded /dcfg_properties() entity-set string in @odata.bind instead of EntitySets.properties
detail: Lines 498 and 544 hardcode the string `/dcfg_properties(...)` for the dcfg_property_id@odata.bind value, while every other reference in this file uses `${EntitySets.properties}`. Risk: if the entity set name ever changes (it won't — see project_properties_not_propertys.md — but the principle applies for any other lookup), this file becomes the place where it silently goes stale. Also breaks the grep pattern that searches for EntitySets.properties to find all consumers.
recommendedFix: Replace both with `'dcfg_property_id@odata.bind': `/${EntitySets.properties}(${currentPropertyId})``. EntitySets is already imported at line 28. Mechanical, low-risk change.

title: uploadPhoto silently swallows getEnvVar and fetch errors
detail: uploadPhoto() (lines 182-197) wraps both the env-var lookup and the fetch in catch blocks that return the dataUrl as-is — meaning on a real failure (Power Automate down, flow URL not configured) the user sees the photo persist in-memory and a toast 'Photo saved' (line 604) but the photo is NEVER saved to SharePoint or Dataverse. Reload the page and the photo is gone. This is the #1 silent-data-loss pattern in field ops.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:182-197 — both `try { flowUrl = await getEnvVar('dcfg_flow_appliance_photo_url'); } catch { /* */ }` and the inner `try { ... } catch { return dataUrl; }` swallow errors. Line 604: `toast.show('ok', '📷 Photo saved');` runs even if upload silently failed.
recommendedFix: Surface failures via toast: change `catch { return dataUrl; }` to `catch (e) { console.warn('uploadPhoto failed:', e); throw new Error('Photo upload failed — check connection'); }` and update handlePrimaryPhoto/handleSerialPhoto callers to await + try/catch + toast.show('err', 'Photo not saved — try again') on rejection. Also surface 'photo URL not configured' if getEnvVar returns null after config has loaded (don't fall back silently).

title: apiPatch .catch(() => {}) on appliance photo URL save swallows errors silently
detail: Lines 602 and 613: after uploading a primary or serial photo, the code patches the appliance row with the new URL using `.catch(() => {})` — discarding any 4xx/5xx error from Dataverse. If the Webapi/dcfg_appliances/fields list ever drifts and dcfg_primary_photo_url / dcfg_serial_photo_url are missing, the toast still says 'Photo saved' but the URL never persisted, leading to silent data loss.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:602 `if (a.guid) await apiPatch(`/${EntitySets.appliances}(${a.guid})`, { dcfg_primary_photo_url: url }).catch(() => {});` and :613 same pattern for dcfg_serial_photo_url.
recommendedFix: Replace `.catch(() => {})` with `.catch(e => { console.error('Photo URL save failed:', e); toast.show('err', 'Photo uploaded but link could not be saved — refresh and retry'); })`. Same fix at both lines.

title: loadCustomers / openCustomer console.warn-only error handling
detail: Both loadCustomers (line 438-446) and openCustomer (line 448-462) catch errors with `console.warn(...)` only — no user-facing toast. The user sees an empty customer list or empty location list with no idea whether the data is empty or the API failed. In the field-ops mobile context this is especially confusing because the network can drop mid-session.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:445 `} catch (e) { console.warn('Customer load failed:', e.message); }` and :460 `} catch (e) { console.warn('Location load failed:', e.message); }`
recommendedFix: Replace both warns with toast surface: `} catch (e) { console.warn('Customer load failed:', e); toast.show('err', 'Could not load customers — check connection'); }` (toast is already imported at line 32). Same fix for openCustomer's location-load catch.

title: updateApplField runs Array.find on appliances array on every keystroke
detail: updateApplField (line 520-533) does `appliances.find(x => x.id === id)` after the optimistic setAppliances. This happens on EVERY keystroke into the appliance text fields (custom_label, brand, location, install_date, serial). For a property with 20 appliances that's 20 lookups per character typed. Not a perf catastrophe but combines with the debounced setTimeout to make the data flow harder to reason about. Bonus issue: the closure reads `appliances` from the render snapshot, so it sees the OLD array (pre-update) — the optimistic update is one step ahead of the lookup.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:520-533 — `setAppliances(prev => prev.map(...)); const a = appliances.find(x => x.id === id);` — note that `appliances` is the captured stale array, not the just-updated one.
recommendedFix: Use the value from the prev callback: `setAppliances(prev => { const updated = prev.map(...); return updated; });` Then derive the GUID from `id` directly (since the parameter IS the appliance id) and patch: `if (!dvCol || !id) return;` (the .guid lookup is unnecessary since id === guid throughout this file). Reduces to a simple O(1) flow.

title: Two separate useEffects with [] deps for appliance types and customer list — could be parallelized
detail: Lines 416 (load appliance type catalog) and 434 (load customer list) both fire on mount as independent effects. They could be parallelized in a single effect with Promise.all to shave one round-trip on cold load. Minor performance polish.
recommendedFix: Combine into one mount effect: `useEffect(() => { (async () => { await Promise.all([loadApplianceTypes(), loadCustomers()]); })(); }, []);` Low priority — only matters on first paint of the field-ops view.
